key_insight: By using sequence-to-function foundation models, the study shows that somatic mutations can be summarized as continuous, gene-level disruption across protein, regulatory, and splicing dimensions rather than only as discrete hotspot drivers.
clinical_relevance: These disruption profiles were associated with overall survival and treatment-stratified outcomes, suggesting a potential way to refine cancer prognosis beyond tumor mutational burden and hotspot status.
method: Applied AlphaGenome and AlphaMissense to score somatic variant effects across 8,800 TCGA patients spanning 33 cancer types.
Aggregated variant-level predictions into patient-gene disruption profiles for transcription, chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and splicing.
Compared disruption patterns with cancer type, tissue of origin, microsatellite instability, and survival outcomes.
evidence_signal: The analysis used 8,800 patients from TCGA across 33 cancer types, and findings were replicated in an independent treatment-annotated cohort.
watch_item: These are model-derived predictions, so clinical utility still needs prospective validation and careful assessment before use in decision-making.
paper_title: Genomic foundation model-derived disruption profiling links somatic mutations to cancer biology and clinical outcomes
